title: This Android agent works your apps on a hidden second screen
summary: An Android agent that taps through your apps on a hidden background screen while you keep using the phone. Mika asks before it spends money, has no server, and sends your screen only to your model provider: https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika
body_markdown:
Letting an agent tap through your phone apps is less useful if you have to hand over the phone while it works. Mika, an open-source Android agent from wangzan101/Mika, does its tapping on a separate background screen. You keep using the phone, and a small live view lets you check in whenever you want.

A task like "what did the group talk about today?" means scrolling a long chat and summarising it, which can take a while, and the phone stays yours the whole time.

## How it drives apps it has never seen

Mika works by looking at the screen and finding buttons the way a person would. There are no app APIs and no per-app integrations. It ships with usage notes for a list of apps and sites, from Gmail, Uber and WhatsApp to Amazon, GitHub and Google Maps, but the project says anything not on the list still works.

Getting there takes some setup. Chat, web and files run on Android 11 or later. Operating other apps needs Android 12 or later, with Android 14+ recommended, because on 14 the background screen has its own focus and does not interfere with your typing on the main screen. You also pair wireless debugging once through a "Set up phone control" wizard. Android turns wireless debugging off when you change Wi-Fi or restart. With your permission, Mika turns it back on by itself. If it still cannot connect, you pair again.

Beyond app control, there is a built-in desktop-class browser that keeps you signed in, a floating capsule you double-tap to send whatever is on screen with a question, schedules like "do this every Friday", and a Linux sandbox per conversation that runs Python, Node and shell on files you send, on arm64 devices. Tools on your computer can hand Mika tasks through a CLI with a skill, or over MCP.

## The two lines that matter for safety

For an agent that can tap anything on your phone, I care most about where it stops. By default Mika runs in Ask mode, which checks with you only before spending money, such as placing an order or paying, and just does everything else. The shopping demo shows the shape: it picks a charger under $30 rated 4.5 stars or more, adds it to the cart and stops before checkout. Logins, verification codes and payments are handed to you, and screens that block screenshots, like payment and password entry, make it ask you to take over.

You can switch to Autonomous mode. Ask mode guards money and nothing else, so messages, greetings to recruiters and posts go out without a check. That is worth knowing before you point it at your messaging apps.

The second thing to check is where your data goes. There is no Mika server. What you say and what is on your screen go only to the model provider you set up, either your own API key or a ChatGPT, xAI or OpenRouter sign-in. API keys and memories are stored encrypted on the phone, conversations stay on the device, and update checks only contact GitHub. So the privacy question moves to your model provider, which now sees your screen.

The project also warns that automating third-party apps and websites may break their terms of service. Its advice is to use your judgment, keep Ask mode on for anything important and check the results.

## Trying it

Download the APK from the Releases page, connect a model under Settings, then run Settings, Recovery and repair, Compatibility self-check. It runs 12 checks in about a minute to tell you whether your phone is up to it. I would run it before spending time on pairing. I would start with a read-only task, like summarising a chat, and watch the live view once before letting it type anything on your behalf.
